classification.difficultyReason: Follow the fully drawn midpoint rearrangement to infer rectangle width and confirm with the familiar trapezium formula.

content.prompt: Here is another way of dissecting a trapezium to find its area. Take the midpoints of the two non-parallel sides and cut off the triangles, as shown. These are then moved up to form a rectangle.

spec.description: Complete actual source givens, perpendicular heights/equality families and mathematical shaded regions retained. Native editable black10pt figure, no derived dimensions.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What is the length x cm of the rectangle?

answer.worked: The two half-width pieces together contribute half the excess base width: $x=7+\tfrac12(15-7)=11$ cm.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the area of the trapezium, using the rectangle.

answer.worked: Rearrangement preserves area, and the rectangle is 11 cm by 6 cm. Its area is $11(6)=66\text{ cm}^2$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Use the usual formula for the area of a trapezium in the first diagram to confirm your answer in part b.

answer.worked: The usual formula gives $A=\tfrac12(7+15)(6)=66\text{ cm}^2$, confirming part b.
